svg.text: BEST FOR: SCORING AGENT TOOL CALLS
FORMAT LINEAGE: Google, Agents Companion whitepaper (Feb 2025)
Grade the Path, Not Just the Answer: Six Trajectory Metrics on One Refund Run
An agent can reach the right answer the wrong way (duplicate calls, skipped policy checks). Google's Agents Companion defines six ways to score the tool-call sequence.
EXPECTED TRAJECTORY (what a correct run calls, in order)
ACTUAL TRAJECTORY (what the agent really called)
SIX TRAJECTORY METRICS FROM THE GOOGLE 'AGENTS COMPANION' WHITEPAPER — COMPUTED FOR THIS RUN
Is the actual sequence identical to the expected one?
Do the expected actions appear in the right order, extra actions allowed?
Are all expected actions present, order ignored?
What fraction of the agent's actions were expected ones?
What fraction of expected actions did the agent perform?
Compliance flows where the order is the policy (KYC,
Most business workflows: order matters, harmless extras are
Research or data-gathering where sequence is irrelevant.
Diagnosing waste (low precision) vs missed steps (low recall)
— the pair you put on a dashboard.
Safety gates: 'did it call check_policy before issue_refund?'
Also grade the outcome with a judge: 'Was the refund issued to the original payment method and confirmed?' — trajectory metrics catch process errors; outcome checks catch wrong results.
Report in-order match + precision + recall together: a 100% in-order run with 0.5 precision is burning tokens on duplicate calls.
